newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PDVSA refining problems may affect Sept gasoline.
newsitem.headline: PDVSA refining problems may affect Sept gasoline.

text.p: The 45,000 barrel per day (bpd) reforming unit in Venezuela's Cardon refinery is still running at minimum output and the problems could affect four cargoes of gasoline due to be exported in September, a source familiar with the refinery's operations said on Tuesday.

Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) declared force majeure on nine cargoes in August and could extend this into September if the problems with the catalytic regenerator are not resolved, he added.

"The reformer is still working at minimum throughput. We have a programme based on the reformer running at 95 octanes for the first 15 days of the month which means there will be no anti- dumping or refomulated for the first three weeks of September," he said.
The Cardon plant normally produces six cargoes of reformulated and anti-dumping spec gasoline every month, mostly for export to the United States.
Each cargo typically carries 230,000 barrels of product.
"We are still in force majeure. We have not withdrawn the force majeure yet," the source added.
A force majeure can be declared when factors outside a company's control affect its performance on a contract, and it remains in force until these factors are resolved.
"We are going to try to accomodate customers by giving them other (loading) windows," the source added.
In August, two and a half cargoes were cancelled, while other customers accepted alternative supplies.
